title: Orion's smallest watch yet cuts its dial from a meteorite
byline: AN About the author Allie Nguyen More by Allie Nguyen →
excerpt: Orion's smallest watch yet slices its dial from real meteorite, pairs it with a Miyota automatic and a tool-less clasp, and starts at $765.

Some dials fake the fancy stuff. This one skips the printing. The dial on Orion’s Hellcat 36 is a thin slice of actual meteorite, so the crisscross pattern grew inside the metal long before anyone cut it. Orion is a small brand out of Wallingford, Pennsylvania, and the Hellcat 36 is the smallest Orion yet.

Two meteorite dials lead the range at $975 a piece.

A Deep Purple dial opens the lineup at $765, and black mother of pearl sits in the middle at $835.

Orion Hellcat 36: Dark Meteorite
Gunmetal meteorite dial with white printed elements · Miyota 9039 automatic · Limited to 20 pieces
Price: $975
Where to buy: Buy at Orion Watches

A pattern nobody can print

Meteorite carries its pattern inside the metal, a woven grid of crystals that formed as the rock cooled in space. A printer can copy the look for a dial blank. The copy still sits flat in a way the real crystal never does, since light moves across the grain as your wrist turns.

The Light Meteorite pairs the pattern with silver print, so its numbers blend into the metal and surface again at certain angles. Dark Meteorite flips the contrast, white print over a gunmetal dial, and Orion capped that run at 20 pieces. The light dial is the quiet one, and the dark dial gets noticed across a desk.

Full Arabic numerals ring the dial with a thin crosshair at the center, a layout borrowed from old field watches. Applied indices mark the cardinal points, cut with enough edge to catch light of their own. The hands run syringe style, wide and lumed to match the field layout. A dotted minute track rings the outer edge, fine enough to disappear until the light catches it.

Vintage size, modern hardware

The case runs 36.5mm wide and 43mm lug to lug, and the whole watch measures 9.9mm thick. Vintage field watches wore these sizes for decades, back before cases started inflating. A smaller wrist finally gets a dial with some ambition behind it. That thinness helps the watch slide under a cuff without a fight.

Orion shoots the Hellcat 36 on a 6.75 inch wrist, and the proportions sell the size fast, with nothing hanging over the edges or looking squeezed.

A Miyota 9039 automatic does the work inside, and a sapphire display caseback puts it on view. Sapphire guards the front as well, the crown screws down, and water resistance reaches 100 meters. BGW9 lume fills the hands and markers, and it glows blue in the dark.

Case36.5mm diameter, 43mm lug to lug, 9.9mm thick
MovementMiyota 9039 automatic
DialLight Meteorite, Dark Meteorite, Deep Purple, or Black Mother of Pearl
CrystalSapphire, front and display caseback
Water resistance100 meters
LumeBGW9, glows blue
CrownScrew down
BraceletFitted end links, tool-less micro adjust clasp, 18mm lug width
Price$765 to $975, depending on the dial

The caseback coating comes with a catch

The display caseback wears an anti-scratch coating, a thin PVD layer that shrugs off scuffs from the bracelet. Orion explains the thinking right on the product page, since a bracelet loves scratching the back of its own watch.

The trade-off is printed there too, because a coated caseback can’t be refinished later. Most brands bury that line. Orion leaves it where buyers read it before paying.

A clasp that adjusts with a push

Most microbrand bracelets need a tool and a steady hand for a size change. The Hellcat 36 clasp adjusts without either, tool-less micro adjustment built into the mechanism. Wrists swell as a day warms up, and one pushed notch fixes the fit in seconds.

The bracelet’s end links are fitted pieces, and Orion recommends a springbar tweezer for swapping them out. Lugs stand 18mm apart, so the strap collection most watch people already own fits this case. Orion sells leather straps in its own store for days when a bracelet feels like too much metal.

Purple saves money, pearl is nearly gone

Deep Purple runs the same case and movement for $765, its dial stamped with a fine triangular pattern, which saves $210 against the meteorite pair.

The color looks almost black at a glance, then the purple shows when the light hits it.

Black mother of pearl lands at $835, and Orion lists only five pieces left in the store.

Pearl varies even more than meteorite does, so buyers can email the brand ahead and ask for a darker or lighter dial. A specific dial then gets picked out by hand. That kind of pick-your-own detail is the fun of buying from a shop this small.

Orion Hellcat 36: Dark Meteorite
36.5mm case at 9.9mm thick · Sapphire front and display caseback · Tool-less micro adjust clasp
Price: $975
Where to buy: Buy at Orion Watches

Buy the Dark Meteorite if a dial nobody else can duplicate sounds worth $975, since the pattern is the entire product here.

Skip the 36.5mm case if your wrist wears big watches well, and take the 39mm Sylph at $725 as the roomier route. This one’s for smaller wrists that keep getting skipped when the fun dials launch.
